scope: Deployed native origin reached by SSH; local read-only discovery, not external ingress/browser acceptance or inference. No credential values or identifiers retained.

claude.id_encoding: Non-claude IDs prefixed claude-fable-5-dd- followed by reversed original; native request handler reverses this for routing.

findings.detail: Plain OpenAI list intentionally strips capabilities to id/object/owned_by/created. Valid minimal OpenAI shape, insufficient rich discovery.
FreeHub ConvertModels calls ModelInfoToPluginAPI with empty vendorID; ownership is blank.
FreeHub defaults absent context to 1,000,000 and absent output to 16,384. These are not verified per-model ceilings.
Codex compatibility synthesizes reasoning levels when no explicit provider constraint exists. Not proof of native upstream efforts.
Generic FreeHub adapter unconditionally sets SupportsTools=true and discards upstream supported_parameters. Kilo Lyria declares no tools upstream but is advertised with tool_calls locally.
Plugin tool capability is copied into Gemini generation method field; tool_calls is not the generateContent operation.
All generic FreeHub models declared Type=chat, including task-specific embedding/audio/image/video identifiers. Listing is not evidence those tasks are exposed or executable by chat adapter.
Claude discovery renames non-Claude IDs into reversible claude-fable-5-dd aliases. All 208 underlying IDs match after decoding, but clients do not see a consistent ID spelling across protocols.

consolidation.normalization: Candidate discovery only: strip known gateway vendor tags, case-fold, strip free pricing suffix; preserve dates/size/reasoning/variant modifiers. Never infer equivalence by fuzzy matching. Version-dot/hyphen differences need explicit alias entries.

additional_review_candidates.reason: Size-qualified provider name; establish same revision and service contract before joining.
Size-qualified provider name; no automatic suffix removal.
Probable spelling aliases inside same vendor, choose one authoritative upstream ID per credential.

implementation_strategy: Correct metadata first in FreeHub vendor conversion; preserve documented supported parameters/modalities and explicit reasoning controls, identify unknown limits, classify non-chat models. Do not substitute Codex template options for provider facts.

Expose truthful additive metadata through native model discovery; use existing registry and model response boundary. No separate proxy or second catalog service. Any serializer change must keep standard clients and native dashboard intact.

Review explicit identity map by publisher/model/revision/variant. Keep thinking/nonthinking, high/fast/turbo, context variants, safety models, quantization variants, virtual auto routers, dated versions and stealth codenames separate unless authoritative equivalence is established.

FreeHub already has per-vendor model aliases and vendor-specific reverse lookup: assign the same approved canonical alias in each vendor. Native built-ins use their own oauth.model-alias channel; compatible API-key lanes use native alias fields. Never use one ambiguous global freehub reverse mapping for different upstream IDs.

Retain existing provider-qualified names during migration. Native fork aliases can keep originals; FreeHub requires a small additive alias-publication change because its current alias replacement removes the qualified name. Resolve same-vendor duplicate upstream IDs deterministically before publishing.

Use native eligible-credential routing for canonical IDs. Respect capabilities, free-only cost policy, account entitlements, provider privacy and cooldowns. Start with shared guaranteed capability intersection and minimum confirmed limits; do not publish a union that routes unsupported options randomly.

Keep one physical dispatch per caller and no same-request replay after rejection. Preserve existing per-credential cooldowns and provider/IP shared limits; retain strict OpenCode quarantine. Initial preferred routes should be accepted for the specific model, not merely a provider with a different live-passed model.

First staged canonical route: nemotron-3.5-lightning through already-passed OpenRouter/Kilo routes. Admit Cline lightning only after model-specific acceptance; do not add NVIDIA merely because its catalog lists a similar model. Then Beam/Kilo+Cline and other reviewed groups. Native Codex should remain preferred over unverified third-party GPT-branded routes.

vercel.rate_limits: No public per-model numbers/ranking proving upstream limits generally stricter. Free Gateway limit and upstream capacity are separate; purchasing credits removes Gateway limits, not provider capacity or model entitlement gates.
vercel.accounts: Keys under same team do not create independent balances/entitlements. Separate legitimate organizations may have their own funding, but independent upstream capacity/free quota is not guaranteed. Vercel AUP explicitly prohibits multiple-account use to circumvent rate limits.

public_upstream_spotcheck.finding: No tools declared upstream; local generic model declares tool_calls and omits audio output modality.
